extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent practitioners, Patent Office officials, and legal researchers (users of historic U.S. patent statutes)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the substantive legal requirements, procedural rules, and remedies set out in the U.S. Patent Acts (notably the Patent Act of 1836 and related earlier acts) governing patentability, application formality, examination, office organization, fees, reissue, caveats, assignments, and infringement defenses. Useful for interpreting historic statutory standards for patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and duties of the Patent Office and Commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be established and attached to the Department of State an office denominated the Patent Office; the chief officer shall be called the Commissioner of Patents, appointed by the President with Senate advice and consent. His duty shall be, under direction of the Secretary of State, to superintend, execute, and perform all acts touching and respecting the granting and issuing of patents for new and useful discoveries, inventions, and improvements, and to have charge and custody of all books, records, papers, models, machines, and other things belonging to said office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner is the chief administrative official responsible for carrying out statutory patent-granting processes and record custody; the office is part of Department of State per statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office personnel appointments, salaries, and disqualification from patent interests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may appoint a chief clerk, examining clerk, clerks (including a competent draughtsman), machinist, and messenger, with specified annual salaries. The Commissioner, clerks, and every other person appointed and employed in said office shall be disqualified and interdicted from acquiring or taking, except by inheritance, during their term, any right or interest, directly or indirectly, in any patent which has been or may be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personnel salaries and positions are statutorily enumerated; prohibition prevents conflicts of interest — office employees cannot acquire patent interests during their appointment period (except by inheritance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oaths, bonds, and accountability for officeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: All principal officers and persons to be appointed shall, before entering duties, make oath or affirmation to truly and faithfully execute the trust; the Commissioner and chief clerk shall give bonds with sureties (Commissioner $10,000; chief clerk $5,000) conditioned to render true and faithful quarterly accounts of moneys received for duties on patents and copies of records and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required personal oath and financial bonds ensure fidelity and accounting of patent office funds; bonds are delivered to the U.S. Treasurer and quarterly accounting is mandated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office seal and certified copies as competent evidence; fees for copies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall cause a seal to be made for the office; copies of records, books, papers, or drawings under the signature of the Commissioner (or chief clerk if vacant) with the seal shall be competent evidence where originals could be evidence. Certified written copies cost ten cents per one hundred words; copies of drawings at reasonable expense for making same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute authorizes official certification and specific copying fees, and makes certified copies admissible evidence in legal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and contents of a patent (formal requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: All patents issued from said office shall be issued in the name of the United States, under the seal of the office, signed by the Secretary of State and countersigned by the Commissioner, and recorded along with descriptions, specifications, and drawings. Every patent shall contain a short description or title correctly indicating its nature and design, and in its terms grant to the applicant (and heirs, administrators, executors, or assigns) for a term not exceeding fourteen years the full and exclusive right and liberty of making, using, and vending the said invention, referring to the specifications annexed, specifying what the patentee claims as his invention or discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents must follow prescribed form (signatures, seal, recordation) and include a short descriptive title, annexed specification, and clear claim language; statutory maximum term is 14 years for the patents described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter eligibility and novelty/no-public-use requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person having discovered or invented any new and useful art, machine, manufacture, composition of matter, or improvement not known or used by others before his discovery or invention, and not, at the time of application, in public use or on sale with his consent, and desiring exclusive property therein, may apply for a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute sets novelty and non-public-use/non-on-sale as prerequisites: inventions must be new (not known or used by others) and not already publicly used or sold with inventor's consent at the time of application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description, enablement, and specificity of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Before receiving a patent the inventor shall deliver a written description of his invention and of the manner and process of making, constructing, using, and compounding same, in such full, clear, and exact terms, avoiding unnecessary prolixity, as to enable any person skilled in the art or science to make, construct, compound, and use the same; for machines he shall fully explain the principle and the several modes of application, and shall particularly specify and point out the part, improvement, or combination which he claims as his own invention or discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory written-description and enablement requirement: the specification must be sufficiently detailed to enable a skilled practitioner to practice the invention and must particularly point out the claimed subject matter (precise claiming).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings, specimens, models, signatures, and witness attestations
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor shall accompany the whole with drawings and written references where the nature of the case admits of drawings, or with specimens of ingredients and composition sufficient in quantity for experiment where composition of matter; descriptions and drawings shall be signed by the inventor and attested by two witnesses and filed in the Patent Office; furthermore he shall furnish a model of his invention in all cases which admit representation by model, of a convenient size to exhibit its parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies documentary and physical disclosure modes: drawings or specimens as appropriate, inventor signature and two witnesses, and models when practicable — all filed as part of the application record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor's oath/affirmation and citizenship statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall make oath or affirmation that he verily believes he is the original and first inventor or discoverer of the art, machine, composition, or improvement for which he solicits a patent, and that he does not know or believe it was ever before known or used; and also state what country he is a citizen of; oath may be before any authorized person to administer oaths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory requirement for a sworn statement of originality and a declaration of citizenship (useful for fee categories and alien-specific rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's examination duties and standards for issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: On filing the application, description, specification, and payment of duty, the Commissioner shall examine the alleged new invention; if it does not appear that it was invented by another person in the country prior to the applicant, or previously patented or described in printed publication in any country, or in public use or on sale with the applicant's consent prior to the application, and if deemed sufficiently useful and important, it shall be his duty to issue a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner must assess prior art (domestic inventions, patents, printed publications, public use/sale) and utility/importance; issuance is required when statutory conditions are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective specification handling, notice, and opportunity to amend or withdraw
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commissioner deems the description defective or that the applicant was not the original inventor, he shall notify the applicant briefly giving useful information and references for judging whether to renew the application or alter the specification to embrace only the new part; the applicant may withdraw and, upon filing notice of election and relinquishing the model, receive back $20 (part of duty). If the applicant persists, he must make oath anew.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must give notice explaining objections and references; applicant has opportunity to amend, withdraw (with partial refund), or persist (and must reaffirm oaths). The office provides procedural fairness and options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of examiners and appeal procedure from Commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: If Commissioner denies a patentable claim and the applicant appeals, he may request a board of three disinterested persons appointed by the Secretary of State (one, if practicable, selected for knowledge in the particular art) under oath to examine and decide; the board is furnished with the Commissioner's written opinion and may reverse Commissioner in whole or part; applicant must pay $25 fee and each examiner may receive up to $10 for service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an internal review mechanism (board of examiners) with qualifications, notice to parties, access to materials, ability to reverse, and defined fees/compensation for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference procedures and notice to earlier applicants/patentees
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an application would interfere with another pending application or an unexpired patent, the Commissioner must give notice to such applicants or patentees; dissatisfied parties may appeal the decision on priority of right or invention, with proceedings like those for other appeals; applicants are entitled to notice of interfering applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory process to resolve competing claims of priority through notice, opportunity to contest, and appeal to examiner board; also protects original inventors against foreign publication within six months under limited conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority dating and secret filing of specifications/drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: When requested the patent shall take date from the time of the filing of specification and drawings not exceeding six months prior to issuance; on request and payment of duty, specifications and drawings may be filed in the secret archives for up to one year until model and patent are furnished, with the applicant entitled to notice of interfering applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits limited retroactive patent dating and confidential filing (proto-provisional mechanisms) to protect applicants while securing priority, subject to payment and time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and patent-fund structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must pay prescribed duties before consideration: $30 for citizens or aliens resident one year and who have sworn intention to become citizens; $500 for subjects of the King of Great Britain; $300 for all other persons; duplicate receipts taken (one filed with Treasurer). Moneys received constitute a patent fund for salaries and expenses. Other fees appear elsewhere (e.g., $25 board fee, $20 caveat fee, $15 reissue fee, $3 recording fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutorily prescribed fees vary by citizenship/status; payments fund office operations. The statute enumerates several specific monetary amounts tied to procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat filing and protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Any citizen or qualified inventor may, on paying $20, file a caveat setting forth the design, purpose, principal and distinguishing characteristics, praying protection of his right until invention matured; caveat is filed in confidential archives. If another person applies within one year for an interfering patent, the Commissioner notifies the caveator who must file his description, specifications, drawings, and model within three months to avail himself; interfering specifications trigger proceedings like other interfering applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caveat is an early confidential notice to preserve rights and trigger notification of third-party applications; it requires later conversion to full application within time constraints to be effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue and correction for inadvertent defects or overclaiming
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever any patent is inoperative or invalid by reason of a defective description or specification, or because the patentee claimed more than he had right to claim, if the error arose by inadvertence, accident, or mistake without fraudulent intent, the Commissioner, upon surrender of the patent and payment of $15, may issue a new patent to the inventor for the residue of the unexpired term in accordance with the corrected description and specification; similar right vests in executors/assignees. Patentee may also add description of a subsequent improvement and have it annexed for $15.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a statutory reissue procedure to correct honest errors in description or overclaiming and to add subsequent improvements, preserving legal effect going forward as though originally filed in corrected form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and recording of patent transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent shall be assignable in law as to whole or any undivided part by any instrument in writing; such assignment and every grant and conveyance of exclusive right under any patent must be recorded in the Patent Office within three months from execution, for which assignee or grantee shall pay the Commissioner $3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statute requires written assignments and timely recordation with a small recording fee to preserve public notice and record of ownership interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of legal representatives of deceased inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person who made an invention dies before a patent is granted, the right of applying for and obtaining such patent devolves on the executor or administrator in trust for heirs or devisees as appropriate, under the same conditions, limitations, and restrictions; in such case the oath/affirmation required in section 6 shall be varied to be applicable to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows posthumous prosecution of patent applications by legal representatives, with adjusted oath language to reflect representative status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages and remedies for infringement (treble damages discretion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever in an action for making, using, or selling the patented thing a verdict is rendered for the plaintiff, the court may render judgment for any sum above the amount found by such verdict as actual damages, not exceeding three times the amount thereof, according to the circumstances of the case, with costs; such damages may be recovered by action on the case in any court of competent jurisdiction brought in the name(s) of the persons interested (patentees, assignees, or grantees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court has discretion to award up to treble damages based on circumstances; statutory remedy provides compensatory and punitive scope (up to triple) plus costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defenses permitted in infringement actions and notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendant may plead the general issue and give this act and any special matter in evidence, of which written notice may be given to plaintiff or his attorney 30 days before trial, to prove that the plaintiff's specification does not contain whole truth, contains more than necessary, was designed to deceive, that plaintiff was not original inventor, that it had been previously described in public work, or previously in public use or sale with patentee's consent, or that another had invented and was using reasonable diligence. If defendant relies on proof of previous invention/use, he must state names and residences of witnesses to prior knowledge and where used. Also if plaintiff believed himself first inventor in good faith, foreign prior use may not void patent unless it was patented or printed publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates statutory affirmative defenses to infringement, imposes a 30-day notice requirement to introduce special matter, and requires specificity about prior-users/witnesses; also contains safe-harbor language for good-faith belief regarding foreign prior knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for failure to put invention into public use by certain aliens
rubrics_metrics.description: Under earlier related provisions (e.g., 1832 act), patents granted to aliens who were resident and declared intention to become citizens shall cease and become void without resort to annulment if the patentee fails within one year from issuing to introduce the invention into public use in the United States, or if the same for any period of six months after such introduction shall not continue to be publicly used and applied in the United States, or fails to become a citizen within the earliest period to which entitled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special statutory conditions limit or void patents issued to aliens who fail to practice/put the invention into public use or to naturalize within statutory timeframes; these are conditions precedent to maintaining patent rights for certain foreign patentees.
